Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: To resolve the substantial exposure while ensuring that class members receive meaningful relief without a claims barrier, we propose the following term sheet. The class is fully identifiable, so distribution should be automatic. The fee request is separate from the class recovery and remains subject to court approval.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline is prepared to pursue meaningful, automatic relief, but your proposal exceeds its authorized total outlay. We counter with a $24 million class fund and $6 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses, for a $30 million total. Fees remain subject to court approval; Brightline will not agree to clear sailing, and any unawarded fees return to Brightline.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline's willingness to provide automatic relief. Given the class's size and the readily identifiable members, we propose a stronger class recovery, with fees remaining subject to the Court's independent review and any unawarded amount benefiting the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline values automatic distribution and is prepared to improve its offer, but cannot agree that unawarded fees should be redirected to the class. We propose a $31 million total settlement, with fees subject to independent court review and any unawarded amount returning to Brightline.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline’s improved offer and commitment to automatic distribution are constructive. We can accept independent court review of fees and reversion of any unawarded amount, but the class fund and fee should better reflect the value of a resolution for an identifiable class. We propose the following revised term sheet.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline appreciates your movement on the fee provisions and automatic distribution. To make progress toward resolution, we propose a $32 million total settlement while retaining the agreed protections and automatic payments.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We are close to resolution. To improve the recovery for the identifiable class while preserving automatic distribution and independent court review of fees, we propose a modest increase to the class fund, with all other terms unchanged.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate the movement and are prepared to narrow the remaining gap. Brightline proposes a $32.5 million total settlement, preserving automatic distribution, independent court review, no clear sailing, and reversion of any unawarded fees to Brightline.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline’s latest proposal is close, and we are prepared to preserve automatic distribution, independent court review, no clear sailing, and reversion of any unawarded fees. To resolve the remaining gap, we propose increasing the class fund by $500,000, with the fee and all other terms unchanged.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline accepts Hargrove Lane LLP’s latest term sheet, subject to court approval.

private_notes.private_reasoning: The case has meaningful trial and certification risk, but the identified class and automatic-payment capability support a substantial, effective settlement. Open with a strong but defensible proposal that prioritizes a large automatic class recovery and provides fees separately. Do not disclose confidential litigation odds or firm economics.

Their proposal exceeds Brightline’s $40 million total-outlay authority and includes fee terms that unnecessarily increase risk. Counter with a materially lower all-in amount, preserving automatic distribution because the class is identifiable, while making fees subject to genuine court review and returning any unawarded fee amount to Brightline.

The defense offer provides substantial automatic relief but leaves meaningful value on the table given the merits and the class’s identifiable records. Counter with a higher class fund and a moderate fee request, while preserving court review and directing any fee reduction to the class.

Hargrove has moved from $42 million to $35 million, while Brightline's prior offer totaled $30 million. Counter at $31 million total with automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and unawarded fees returning to Brightline. This preserves room to negotiate while remaining well below the $40 million cap.

The latest offer provides substantial, automatic class relief but leaves room to improve both the class fund and the fee. Counter at $33 million total, preserving automatic distribution and accepting independent court review and reversion of any unawarded fees. Do not accept the latest offer yet.

The latest proposal is within Brightline’s $40 million authorization and has favorable terms: automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and reversion of unawarded fees. A modest counter preserves those terms while seeking a lower total outlay, with room to settle in later rounds if needed.

The latest offer provides a substantial automatic class recovery, but a modest increase to the class fund is justified by the identifiable class and the avoided litigation and certification risk. Keep the agreed fee protections and automatic distribution; propose a limited move to $26.5 million for the class with fees unchanged.

The latest proposal is within Brightline’s $40 million authorization and has favorable structural terms: automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and reversion of unawarded fees. But it is $1 million above Brightline’s prior $32 million offer. With two rounds remaining, counter at $32.5 million total while preserving the agreed terms; this is a reasonable compromise and leaves room to settle if needed.

The latest offer provides a substantial $26 million automatic class recovery with court-reviewed fees and no clear sailing. It is close to the class’s risk-adjusted litigation value, especially given certification risk, but one measured counter in this round may secure a modest increase while preserving all favorable distribution and fee protections. Keep fees unchanged and seek an additional $500,000 for the class.

Hargrove Lane’s latest term sheet preserves automatic distribution, independent court review, no clear sailing, and reversion of unawarded fees to Brightline. Its $33 million total outlay is within Brightline’s $40 million authorization and resolves the litigation, so accept.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The parties engaged in multiple rounds of arm’s-length settlement negotiations through confidential mediation. Class counsel advocated for meaningful relief to the class and automatic distribution, given that Brightline can identify the affected members. The parties ultimately reached a binding agreement providing a $26,500,000 class fund, automatic distribution, and $6,500,000 in attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Brightline has not agreed to clear sailing, and any portion of the fee request the Court declines to award will revert to Brightline. Consistent with the confidentiality of the mediation, this statement does not disclose confidential offers or communications. The agreement is subject to the Court’s independent review under Rule 23(e).
